title: Exact metric conversions
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: When a recipe, a science lab or a trip abroad switches between inches and centimeters or pounds and kilograms, these are the numbers behind every conversion chart. Most of them grow out of just two: the inch (2.54 cm) and the pound (0.45359237 kg).

How to hold it: Learn the two roots first, the inch and the pound, and derive the rest: a foot is 12 inches, so 12 x 2.54 = 30.48 cm. Working it out once is a strong encoding step, and it turns ten facts into two facts plus reasoning. Then use rounded versions for everyday sense (a mile is about 1.6 km, a kilogram about 2.2 pounds) and the exact ones when it matters. Chunk as length, weight, volume, temperature.
